lauren_s: Hey team, customer on Dedicated (pool id: rp-8a3f) is seeing intermittent 429s even though they have a steady reserved throughput configured. Started ~08:12 UTC. They say traffic is well under their committed qps. request_id: r-0a1b2c3d.
lauren_s: Quick details: model=gpt-large-v1, route=/v1/generate, reserved_capacity=120 qps, observed 429 spikes to ~30s every few minutes. No auth errors.
ajay_sre: thanks — can you paste an example of the client pattern? steady vs bursts? any periodic cron jobs?
lauren_s: customer claims steady: many small concurrent requests (avg 50ms prompt processing), ~100 concurrent connections. No cron. They attached traces but here's the minimal repro curl they used:
lauren_s: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer SK_XXXX' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-v1","input":"hello","max_tokens":50}' \\n  -v
```
lauren_s: Their traffic profile shows requests arriving in microbursts (many simultaneous small requests) that the token-bucket on the gateway is smoothing to bursts.
matt_product: Is this the reserved-pool token-bucket or a downstream global limiter? Could be gateway per-route limiter + reserved pool interaction.
ajay_sre: grabbing logs for rp-8a3f... small excerpt: ```
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] pool=rp-8a3f req=r-0a1b2c3d conn=12 status=200 latency=48ms
[2026-03-15T08:12:07Z] pool=rp-8a3f req=r-0a1b2c3e conn=125 status=429 rl_reason=token_bucket_empty
[2026-03-15T08:12:08Z] pool=rp-8a3f req=r-0a1b2c3f conn=130 status=429 rl_reason=reserved_headroom_exhausted
[2026-03-15T08:12:11Z] pool=rp-8a3f req=r-0a1b2c40 conn=18 status=200 latency=52ms
```
ajay_sre: pattern shows bursts where concurrency spikes past the basket window — the reserved pool will smooth by design; if client concurrency is high and token refill window is coarse, you'll see transient 429s.
billing_kate: customer is concerned because these 429s are counted against SLA billing credits. Is that expected?
matt_product: We should separate two things: (1) customer-facing SLA for provisioned qps (committed throughput) — we allow short smoothing bursts but if gateway-level token bucket rejects because of microburst, it can still surface 429 even if average qps < committed. (2) our billing credits for SLA breaches are triggered by sustained underprovisioning per policy. Short transient 429s likely won't trigger credits but customer confusion is valid.
lauren_s: customer asks for recommended mitigations + steps to reproduce on our side.
ajay_sre: repro steps I'd run from our infra: 1) run a client that opens N parallel connections and loops requests with small payloads (we use wrk or vegeta). 2) target qps ~80% of reserved but with concurrency set high to create microbursts. Example vegeta command: ```bash
echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate","body":"{\"model\":\"gpt-large-v1\",\"input\":\"hi\"}"}' > targets.json
vegeta attack -targets=targets.json -rate=96 -connections=200 -timeout=2s | vegeta report
```
ajay_sre: On our side run a quick log filter to correlate token refills: ```bash
rg "rp-8a3f" /var/log/redwood/gateway.log | sed -n '1,200p' | rg "token_bucket|reserved_headroom" -n
```
matt_product: Short-term mitigation for customer: reduce client concurrency (reuse connections and add small jitter), or set client-side leaky-bucket to smooth bursts. For a platform-side fix: consider increasing pool burst window or tune token refill rate for rp-8a3f.
lauren_s: Customer asked if we can temporarily increase burst headroom for them while we investigate. ok to do for an escalated customer?
jay_sre: (ajay_sre) I'll propose a controlled bump: increase pool burst_capacity from 20% -> 40% for 30 minutes and monitor. Need approval from product for SLA implications.
matt_product: I'm fine with a targeted bump if we add a guardrail: enable detailed tracing + set an automatic rollback after 30m if overall cluster pressure > 70%. Also annotate billing to not count transient 429s against SLA for that window.
billing_kate: I'll flag the billing side to ignore credit triggers for that customer for the timeframe. Need internal ticket number for audit.
lauren_s: I ran the vegeta repro on a repro instance and I can reproduce ~10s windows of 429s every few minutes. Will attach the full trace.
lauren_s: trace snippet shows gateway rejecting at the token-bucket layer: ```
gateway:rl decision=reject reason=token_bucket_quota_exhausted pool=rp-8a3f tokens_left=0 refill_interval_ms=500 window=1000
```
ajay_sre: that refill_interval_ms=500 with high concurrency explains it. We can either decrease refill interval or raise bucket size. Both impact smoothing behavior.
matt_product: Longer term, we should add an explicit mapping table that aligns reserved pool configs with SLA semantics so customers understand microburst behavior. Also doc update.
lauren_s: Customer requested exact config changes and a timeline. Proposed plan: 1) short bump as ajay suggested (30m) 2) monitor and collect traces 3) if passes, schedule a safe config tweak (increase burst window) during low-traffic hours 4) doc + onboarding note.
ajay_sre: I'll create an internal runbook PR with commands/rollback and post here once done.
deploy-bot: scheduled config change rp-8a3f burst_capacity bump -> 40% starting in 10m, auto-rollback in 30m. ticket=INC-2026-837
lauren_s: thanks all, I'll reply to customer with the mitigation + repro guidance and confirm billing won't penalize transient 429s.
billing_kate: confirmed we'll waive SLA credit triggers for ticket=INC-2026-837 window.
matt_product: action items: ajay create runbook + telemetry query, lauren update customer, billing_kate add waiver note, and I'll follow up on doc update.
lauren_s: noted, closing loop once bump completes and we have metrics. :thumbsup:
